questions.scenario: An online retailer's customer-support resolution agent runs on the Messages API with tools for order lookup, refunds, and escalation. To control context, the application replaces older turns with a model-written summary every 20 turns. In long cases, after two or three summaries, the agent says 'your refund of about $1,200' when the customer was promised $1,240.50, loses one of two order numbers, and forgets that the customer asked for delivery before 14 March. 14% of escalated cases reach humans with at least one wrong amount or date. The team must keep summarizing because cases run to 150+ turns. What is the most effective change?
options: Keep a structured case-facts object (order IDs, amounts, dates, statuses, customer expectations) outside the summary and include it in every request.
Summarize every 40 turns instead of every 20, so each summary condenses fewer times and exact amounts survive longer.
Replace the custom summarization with context editing that clears old tool results once the conversation passes 100,000 tokens.
Ask the summarizer to 'preserve all numbers, dates, and order IDs exactly' and keep the current every-20-turns schedule.
questions.why_correct: Los datos transaccionales no deberían pasar por el resumen. La doc recomienda llevar la información de estado en un formato estructurado como JSON. Un bloque de 'case facts' que viaja en cada request, fuera del historial resumido, conserva montos, IDs y fechas exactos.

why_wrong.1: Retrasa la pérdida pero no la evita: con 150 turnos igual hay varios resúmenes encadenados.
why_wrong.2: Context editing limpia resultados de tools, no los turnos del cliente donde está la promesa ni la fecha; resuelve otro problema.
why_wrong.3: Es guidance sobre el resumidor: mejora algo, pero cada resumen vuelve a reescribir los datos y puede volver a redondear.

questions.rule: Montos, IDs y fechas → objeto de estado estructurado en cada request, fuera del resumen.
questions.source_quote: Use structured formats for state data: When tracking structured information (such as test results or task status), use JSON or other structured formats to make schema requirements explicit to Claude.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices. Prompting best practices: estado en formatos estructurados (JSON). Cita textual; context editing solo limpia tool results. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A telecom's support agent calls a `get_order` tool that returns the full order record from the billing system: 48 fields including internal routing codes, warehouse bin IDs, and audit timestamps. The agent only uses about 5 of them (status, items, amounts, ship date, return eligibility). Average cases make 25 lookups, and input tokens per request grow by roughly 2,500 with each one. Quality reviews show the agent occasionally quoting internal codes to customers and missing the return-eligibility flag. The billing API cannot be changed, but the team owns the tool implementation. What change addresses the root cause?
options: Enable prompt caching on the conversation so the repeated order records cost less on every subsequent request.
Enable context editing with `clear_tool_uses_20250919` so older `get_order` results are cleared from the prompt.
Make the tool implementation return only the fields the agent needs, with stable identifiers, instead of the full 48-field record.
Add to the system prompt: 'Ignore internal fields in order records and never mention routing codes or bin IDs to customers.'
questions.why_correct: La doc pide diseñar las respuestas de las tools para que devuelvan solo información de alta señal: los campos que Claude necesita para su próximo paso. Las respuestas infladas gastan contexto y le cuesta más encontrar lo importante. Recortar en la implementación de la tool ataca la causa.

why_wrong.0: El caché cambia lo que pagás, no cuánto ocupa: los 48 campos siguen en el contexto.
why_wrong.1: Casi: limpia resultados viejos, pero cada lookup nuevo entra igual con 48 campos, y el ruido sigue en los resultados recientes.
why_wrong.3: Es una instrucción para ignorar ruido que igual está en el contexto; no baja tokens ni garantiza nada.

questions.rule: Tool que devuelve de más → recortá en la tool. Solo campos de alta señal.
questions.source_quote: include only the fields Claude needs to reason about its next step. Bloated responses waste context and make it harder for Claude to extract what matters.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/define-tools. Define tools: devolver solo los campos que Claude necesita. Cita textual. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A bank's support agent uses context editing (beta header `context-management-2025-06-27`) with the `clear_tool_uses_20250919` strategy, default `trigger` and `keep`. Early in each case the agent calls `get_refund_policy`, which returns the policy that applies to the customer's account tier. In long cases, once the prompt passes the trigger, that result is replaced with a placeholder; afterwards the agent misstates refund windows in 7% of long cases. Bulk results from `search_transactions` must keep being cleared because they dominate token usage. What is the most targeted fix?
options: Raise `keep` from 3 to 10 tool uses so that more recent tool results, including the policy, survive each clearing pass.
Add `get_refund_policy` to `exclude_tools` so its tool uses and results are never cleared while other results still are.
Set `clear_tool_inputs` to `true` so only the tool call parameters are removed and the policy text itself stays in place.
Raise the `trigger` to 200,000 input tokens so clearing starts later and the policy remains in context for most cases.
questions.why_correct: `exclude_tools` es la lista de tools cuyos usos y resultados nunca se limpian, pensada para conservar contexto importante. La política queda siempre disponible y `search_transactions` se sigue limpiando como antes.

why_wrong.0: `keep` conserva los N usos más recientes; la política se pidió al principio, así que tarde o temprano igual sale.
why_wrong.2: `clear_tool_inputs: true` borra TAMBIÉN los parámetros de las llamadas, además de los resultados; no protege el texto de la política.
why_wrong.3: Solo posterga el problema y deja crecer el contexto con los resultados masivos.

questions.rule: Resultado de tool que siempre tiene que quedar → `exclude_tools`. `keep` es por recencia.
questions.source_quote: List of tool names whose tool uses and results should never be cleared. Useful for preserving important context.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing. Context editing: exclude_tools, keep=3 por recencia, clear_tool_inputs borra también parámetros. Tabla de parámetros verificada; cita textual. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A commercial-lending team extracts covenant terms from 60–120 page loan agreements on the Messages API. The prompt currently reads: system role, then 'Extract every financial covenant and its threshold. Use the schema below,' then the schema and two examples, and finally the full agreement text (about 70,000 tokens). Accuracy is good for covenants near the start and the end of agreements but drops sharply for covenants in the middle sections; across 200 test agreements, recall is 74%. The team cannot split agreements into separate calls because covenants reference definitions elsewhere in the document. What change is most likely to improve recall?
options: Repeat the extraction instruction every 10,000 tokens inside the agreement text so it stays close to every section.
Move the two examples to the end of the prompt, after the agreement, so the model sees them right before answering.
Raise `max_tokens` so the model has enough room to list every covenant, including the ones in the middle sections.
Put the agreement at the top of the prompt, above the instructions, schema, and examples, and put the query at the end.
questions.why_correct: La doc recomienda poner los documentos largos arriba del prompt, por encima de la consulta, las instrucciones y los ejemplos, y dejar la pregunta al final: en pruebas mejora la calidad hasta un 30%, sobre todo con entradas complejas. Acá el prompt tiene el orden invertido.

why_wrong.0: Partir el documento con instrucciones repetidas no está documentado y puede confundir la estructura del contrato.
why_wrong.1: Mueve los ejemplos, pero el documento sigue debajo de la consulta; no aplica la recomendación completa.
why_wrong.2: El problema no es que la respuesta se corte; es la ubicación de la información en una entrada larga.

questions.rule: Long context: documento arriba, instrucciones y pregunta al final.
questions.source_quote: Queries at the end can improve response quality by up to 30 percent in tests, especially with complex, multidocument inputs.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices. Prompting best practices: long docs arriba, query al final, hasta 30%. Cita textual. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: To cut costs, a travel company's chat assistant on the Messages API was changed to send only the system prompt and the latest user message on each request, plus a `conversation_id` the team added to `metadata`, expecting the platform to retrieve earlier turns. Input tokens fell 80%, but the assistant now asks customers for their booking reference again on almost every turn and contradicts what it said two messages earlier. Conversations average 30 turns. The team still needs to reduce token usage. What is the correct approach?
options: Send the full conversation history on every request, and keep it within budget with compaction and trimmed tool results.
Keep sending only the latest message, but enable prompt caching keyed on `conversation_id` so earlier turns can be retrieved.
Move to the Message Batches API, which keeps the conversation state between requests that share the same custom ID.
Send the latest message plus the previous one, which is enough short-term memory for most booking conversations.
questions.why_correct: La Messages API es stateless: siempre se manda el historial completo. No hay memoria del lado del servidor por `conversation_id`. Para ahorrar tokens se gestiona el historial (compaction, recortar resultados de tools), no se lo saca.

why_wrong.1: El caché abarata prefijos que vos mismo mandás; no recupera turnos que no enviaste.
why_wrong.2: Batches es procesamiento asincrónico de requests independientes; tampoco guarda estado de conversación.
why_wrong.3: Una ventana tan chica pierde datos del principio, como la referencia de reserva; es el mismo problema en menor escala.

questions.rule: Messages API = stateless. Toda opción con memoria del lado del servidor es falsa.
questions.source_quote: The Messages API is stateless, which means that you always send the full conversational history to the API.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/working-with-messages. Working with messages: API stateless, historial completo. Cita textual. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: An insurance company's claims-support agent uses API server-side compaction with the default summary. Conversations can last days. QA found that after compaction the agent often forgets commitments it made early on, for example 'we will call you back by Friday with the adjuster's decision', and customer preferences such as 'contact only by email'. Recent turns are fine. Complaints about broken promises rose 22% after compaction was enabled. The team wants to keep compaction because cases exceed the context window. What is the best next step?
options: Switch to compaction that keeps recent turns, so the last few turns reach Claude word for word after each compaction.
Write a custom summarization prompt that requires the summary to preserve commitments made and customer preferences.
Disable compaction and send the full raw history, relying on a larger context window model for the longest cases.
Enable context editing to clear old tool results, so that more of the window stays available for the conversation text.
questions.why_correct: La doc ofrece escribir tu propio prompt de resumen cuando el resumen por defecto pierde algo que un turno posterior necesita; tu prompt reemplaza al default. Acá lo que se pierde son compromisos y preferencias de turnos viejos, así que hay que pedir explícitamente que el resumen los conserve.

why_wrong.0: Casi: conservar los turnos recientes no ayuda, porque los compromisos están en turnos viejos, justo los que se resumen.
why_wrong.2: Los casos ya superan la ventana; y con más tokens la precisión baja (context rot).
why_wrong.3: Libera espacio pero no cambia qué conserva el resumen; los compromisos se siguen perdiendo.

questions.rule: El resumen por defecto pierde algo que necesitás → prompt de resumen propio.
questions.source_quote: Write your own summarization prompt: when the default summary drops something a later turn needs. Your prompt replaces the default one.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction. Compaction: prompt de resumen propio reemplaza el default; también existe `instructions` en compaction por umbral. Cita textual. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A SaaS company's support agent includes a 150,000-token product knowledge base at the start of every request, marked with `cache_control`, and caching works: cache reads are high and cost per request dropped 70%. Long conversations now fail with HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error` ('prompt is too long') once the history grows, and answer quality on recent questions has declined. An engineer argues that cached tokens 'don't count anymore' and proposes caching the conversation history too. The model cannot be changed. What should the team do?
options: Retrieve only the knowledge-base sections relevant to each turn and compact older history, since cached tokens still occupy the window.
Add `cache_control` breakpoints to the conversation history as well, so the growing history also stops counting toward the limit.
Move the knowledge base from the first user message into the system prompt, which is not counted toward the context window.
Extend the cache TTL so the knowledge base stays cached across long conversations and stops counting toward the window.
questions.why_correct: Los prefijos en caché siguen ocupando la ventana de contexto: el caché cambia lo que pagás, no si cuentan. Para que entre y además mejore la calidad, hay que mandar menos: solo las secciones relevantes de la base y el historial viejo compactado.

why_wrong.1: Cachear más baja el costo pero no el tamaño; el 400 sigue apareciendo.
why_wrong.2: Todo lo que va en la request cuenta, incluido el system prompt.
why_wrong.3: El TTL solo afecta cuánto dura el caché; no saca tokens de la ventana.

questions.rule: Prompt caching = más barato, no más chico. Lo cacheado ocupa la ventana igual.
questions.source_quote: Cached prompt prefixes still occupy the context window: prompt caching changes what you pay for those tokens, not whether they count.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows. Context windows: los prefijos cacheados siguen ocupando la ventana. Cita textual. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A developer-tools company built a code-assistant chat on the Messages API with on-demand compaction. Users iterate on a single function over many turns: they paste the current version, Claude proposes a diff, they paste test output. After each compaction, the summary paraphrases the last few turns ('the user shared an updated version of the function with a fix to the loop'), and Claude then edits a version of the code that no longer exists. Older turns are fine as summaries. The team needs the exact recent code and test output to reach Claude after compaction. Which option fits best?
options: Write a custom summarization prompt telling the summarizer to copy all code blocks from the conversation into the summary.
Disable compaction and instead clear old tool results with context editing whenever the prompt exceeds 100,000 tokens.
Ask users to paste the full current function again in every message so the latest code never depends on the summary.
Use compaction that keeps recent turns, so the last few turns reach Claude word for word and only older turns are summarized.
questions.why_correct: La doc describe esta variante para cuando los últimos turnos tienen que llegar a Claude palabra por palabra: el resumen cubre solo los turnos viejos. Es exactamente el caso: código y tests recientes textuales, el resto resumido.

why_wrong.0: Casi: un prompt propio puede pedir el código, pero sigue siendo un resumen generado; meter todo el código histórico infla el resumen y no garantiza la versión exacta.
why_wrong.1: Acá no hay tool results que limpiar: el contenido son mensajes del usuario. Resuelve otro problema.
why_wrong.2: Traslada el problema al usuario y llena el contexto con copias repetidas.

questions.rule: Turnos recientes que tienen que llegar textuales → compaction que mantiene los turnos recientes.
questions.source_quote: Compaction that keeps recent turns: when the last few turns must reach Claude word for word. The summary covers only the older turns.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction. Compaction: variante que mantiene los turnos recientes textuales. Cita textual; buen par casi-correcto con A. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A compliance-sensitive internal research agent uses context editing with `clear_tool_uses_20250919`. Worried that their stored history would drift from what Claude actually saw, the team built a 'sync' step: after each response, it rewrites the local conversation history by replacing old tool results with placeholder text, mirroring the server-side clearing. Two problems followed: auditors found the retained logs no longer contain full tool outputs, which policy requires, and engineers keep fixing bugs in the sync code. What should the team do?
options: Keep the sync step but write the original tool outputs to a separate audit table before replacing them with placeholders.
Switch from context editing to client-side clearing, so the local history and what Claude sees are always identical.
Remove the sync step and keep managing the full, unmodified history locally, because context editing is applied server-side.
Set `clear_tool_inputs` to `false` so the local history keeps the tool calls and only the results need to be synchronized.
questions.why_correct: Context editing se aplica del lado del servidor antes de que el prompt llegue a Claude. Tu app mantiene el historial completo sin modificar y no necesita sincronizarse con la versión editada. Sin el sync, los logs quedan completos para auditoría y desaparece el código con bugs.

why_wrong.0: Mantiene el código innecesario y sus bugs; arregla la auditoría con más complejidad en vez de quitar la causa.
why_wrong.1: Mover la limpieza al cliente justamente modifica el historial guardado y te hace responsable de lo que hoy hace el servidor.
why_wrong.3: `false` ya es el default y solo controla si se limpian los parámetros de las llamadas; no tiene que ver con sincronizar.

questions.rule: Context editing es server-side: tu historial local queda completo y no se sincroniza.
questions.source_quote: Context editing is applied server-side before the prompt reaches Claude. Your client application maintains the full, unmodified conversation history. You do not need to sync your client state with the edited version.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing. Context editing: server-side, el cliente mantiene historial completo sin sync. Cita textual; clear_tool_inputs default false. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A B2B support platform moved its account-management agent to a 1M-token context model and turned off all summarization, reasoning that 'everything now fits'. Conversations with large enterprise customers now reach 500,000–700,000 tokens over several weeks. Requests still succeed, but evaluations show the agent misremembering contract terms agreed early in the thread and contradicting earlier commitments in 18% of long conversations, versus 4% before the change. Latency and cost also rose. The team wants quality back without losing important history. What is the best approach?
options: Raise `max_tokens` so the agent has more room to reason over the long history before writing each answer.
Enable prompt caching on the history so the large conversations become cheaper and faster on every turn.
Repeat the key contract terms at the end of every user message so they are always close to the question.
Keep the active context small with compaction and carry agreed terms in a structured state block on each request.
questions.why_correct: Más contexto no es automáticamente mejor: a medida que crecen los tokens, baja la precisión y el recuerdo (context rot). La compaction mantiene chico el contexto activo, y un bloque de estado estructurado conserva los términos acordados exactos.

why_wrong.0: `max_tokens` limita la salida; no cambia cuánto contexto tiene que procesar ni la degradación.
why_wrong.1: Baja costo y latencia, pero los tokens siguen en la ventana y la calidad sigue cayendo.
why_wrong.2: Funciona a medias: depende de mandar a mano los términos y sigue arrastrando 700k tokens de historial.

questions.rule: Ventana grande ≠ usarla toda. Contexto chico y curado + estado estructurado.
questions.source_quote: A larger context window allows the model to handle more complex and lengthy prompts, but more context isn’t automatically better. As token count grows, accuracy and recall degrade, a phenomenon known as context rot.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows. Context windows: context rot, más contexto no es mejor. Cita textual. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A research agent processes long batches of documents through tool calls and uses both prompt caching and context editing with `clear_tool_uses_20250919` (default `trigger`, `keep: 3`). After enabling context editing, the input-token bill went up 35% instead of down. Usage logs show cache writes on almost every request once the conversation passes the trigger, each time a small, older tool result is cleared. The team wants to keep clearing old tool results but stop paying for constant cache rewrites. Which configuration change addresses this?
options: Set `keep` to 0 so every old tool result is cleared in a single pass and the cache is invalidated only one time.
Set `clear_at_least` so each clearing pass removes enough tokens to make the cache invalidation worthwhile.
Lower the `trigger` to 30,000 input tokens so clearing happens earlier, while the prompt is still small and cheap.
Disable prompt caching for the conversation so clearing tool results no longer causes any cache write costs.
questions.why_correct: Limpiar tool results invalida el prefijo cacheado. La doc dice que limpies suficientes tokens para que valga la pena y que uses `clear_at_least` para asegurar un mínimo por pasada: si no se puede limpiar ese mínimo, la estrategia no se aplica y el caché se conserva.

why_wrong.0: `keep: 0` borra también los resultados recientes que Claude todavía necesita, y no impide nuevas invalidaciones en cada request siguiente.
why_wrong.2: Limpiar antes y más seguido multiplica las invalidaciones; empeora el costo.
why_wrong.3: Elimina la factura de escritura de caché perdiendo todo el ahorro de lecturas; cambia un problema por otro.

questions.rule: Context editing + caching → `clear_at_least` para que cada limpieza justifique romper el caché.
questions.source_quote: To account for this, clear enough tokens to make the cache invalidation worthwhile. Use the `clear_at_least` parameter to ensure a minimum number of tokens is cleared each time.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing. Context editing: clear_at_least para que valga romper el caché; si no alcanza el mínimo la estrategia no se aplica. Cita textual. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.
